cues.zh: 在《星际迷航》里，传送机能把你从一个地方送到另一个地方，省下了穿梭机的燃料（还有特效预算）。
cues.en: In Star Trek, the transporter moves you from one spot to another, saving on shuttle fuel (and special effects budgets).

cues.zh: 在剧集设定里，它是“最安全的旅行方式”。
cues.en: In-universe, it's 'the safest way to travel'.

cues.zh: 没错，*有时候*，在极少数情况下，会有两个人死得惨不忍睹、面目全非……
cues.en: Yes, *sometimes*, two guys die horrible, mutilated deaths under rare circumstances...

cues.zh: ……但每天早晨，数以万亿计的人传送去上班，连个嗝都不打。
cues.en: ...but trillions of individuals transport to work every morning without a hiccup.

cues.zh: 可是，万一传送机并没有声称的那么安全呢……
cues.en: But, what if the transporter isn't as safe as claimed...

cues.zh: ……万一死亡率不是近乎为零，而是百分之百呢……
cues.en: ...what if the death rate isn't point almost nothing percent, but one-hundred percent...

cues.zh: ……因为传送机就是个自杀盒子。
cues.en: ...because the transporter is a suicide box.

cues.zh: 首先，传送机是怎么工作的？
cues.en: First, how does the transporter work?

cues.zh: 有技术手册，一页又一页，全是好笑到过分具体的细节……
cues.en: There are technical manuals, with pages and pages of hilariously over-specific details...

cues.zh: 可说的东西又*少得可怜*。
cues.en: that yet say *so little*.

cues.zh: 《星际迷航》最大的特点就是一贯地不一致，不过，取最常见的设定来看：
cues.en: Star Trek is nothing if not consistently inconsistent, but, taking the most common elements:

cues.zh: 首先，传送机会把你扫描到夸克级别，拆解你的原子，再把这些碎片送到目的地重新组装。
cues.en: First, the transporter scans you down to the quark, takes apart your atoms and sends the pieces of you to the destination for reassembly.

cues.zh: 但是，传送出来的真的还是*你*吗？还是一个自以为是你的复制品？
cues.en: But, is it *you* on the other end? Or a copy that thinks it's you?

cues.zh: 那么，“你”究竟*是*什么？
cues.en: Well, who *is* you?

cues.zh: 这是个超级宏大的问题，但我们不妨用严谨的科学态度来看待：
cues.en: That's a hell of a big question, but let's try to be good scientists about it:

cues.zh: ……我们不假设你身上存在某种无法被测量的神奇部分。
cues.en: ...we don't assume there's a magic part of you that can't be measured.

cues.zh: 毕竟，如果它无法被测量，那就意味着从定义上讲它无法影响任何事物。
cues.en: After all, if it can't be measured, that means by definition it can't affect anything.

cues.zh: 所以用奥卡姆剃刀把它剔除掉，我们把你看作你表现出来的样子：一堆自以为是“你”的原子集合。
cues.en: So Occam's Razor it away and we take you as you seem to be: a collection of atoms arranged to think they're you.

cues.zh: 而且因为传送后的原子排列和传送前完全一致……
cues.en: And because the arrangement of atoms in post-transport you is exactly the same as pre-transport...

cues.zh: ……那你肯定就是你。结案。
cues.en: ...you must be you. Case closed.

cues.zh: 但是……你心里可能总还是会犯嘀咕，觉得踏进传送仪后的实际体验会是……
cues.en: But… You might still have this nagging feeling that your experience of stepping into the transporter will be...

cues.zh: ……一声奇怪的响动，一道强光——然后是永恒的虚无……
cues.en: ...a funny sound, a bright light -- then nothingness eternal..

cues.zh: ……而在星球表面，一个全新的生命，带着你死前那一刻的全部记忆……
cues.en: ...while down on the planet, a brand-new life, complete with all your memories up to the moment before your death

cues.zh: ……凭空出现，并以为自己就是你……
cues.en: ...popped into existence and assumed it's you...

cues.zh: *不然它还能怎么想？*
cues.en: *How could it otherwise?*

cues.zh: 它的寿命和这次任务一样短暂……
cues.en: It lives a life as short as the mission...

cues.zh: ……接着，一个拥有你们俩记忆的全新生物回到了飞船上。
cues.en: ...and a new creature with the memories of you both makes it back to the ship.

cues.zh: 如果真是这样，把这乘上所有星系、所有飞船里的所有生命……
cues.en: If true, multiply this by all the life forms in all the ships in all the star systems...

cues.zh: ……这项传送技术就成了一场无声的大屠杀……
cues.en: ...and this transport technology is a silent holocaust...

cues.zh: ……这也让随便一集《星际迷航》看起来都变得格外阴暗。
cues.en: ...which makes an average episode of 'Trek rather grim watching.

cues.zh: 要是船员坐了涡轮电梯而不是点对点传送，甚至都算得上是一件幸事。
cues.en: And it's a small mercy when a crew member takes the turbolift rather than site-to-site transport.

cues.zh: 不过话说回来，测量数据都没问题，也许只是我们想多了，而且去赖莎星度假已经快迟到了，赶紧站进去吧。
cues.en: But again, the measurements check out so perhaps we're being paranoid and we're already late for our holiday on Risa so just step inside already.

cues.zh: 但原子重组是乐观版本，传送器不可能真这么运作……
cues.en: But atom reassembly is the optimistic version and can't be how the transporter really works...

cues.zh: ……因为有时事故会把两名船员合为一个——或者把一个人拆成两个。
cues.en: ...because sometimes accidents combine two crew into one - or split one into two.

cues.zh: 你体内的原子不足以再造出一个你，所以传送器必须把原子转化为能量，再把能量转化为原子。
cues.en: There aren't enough atoms in you to make a second you, so the transporter has to be turning atoms into energy and energy into atoms.

cues.zh: 你被摧毁，用来给电池充电，然后被重新创造出来。
cues.en: You are destroyed, used to charge a battery, then recreated anew.

cues.zh: 这看起来真的像死亡。
cues.en: This really seems like death.

cues.zh: 但房间里的哲学专业学生现在*迫不及待*想提“忒修斯之船”——那好吧。
cues.en: But the philosophy majors in the room are *dying* to bring up "The Ship of Theseus" now -- so fine.

cues.zh: 你带着这艘船去冒险。随着部件磨损，你逐一替换，直到最终没有一块是原装的。
cues.en: You take this ship on an adventure. As parts get worn, you replace each until eventually no piece is original.

cues.zh: 当你回来时，“忒修斯之船”还是你离开时的那艘“忒修斯之船”吗？
cues.en: When you return is the "Ship of Theseus" still the same "Ship of Theseus" you left on?

cues.zh: 似乎是——而这正是你身体每天通过进食（引入新原子）和排泄（失去原子）在做的事。
cues.en: Seems so - and this is what your body does daily via eating (bringing in new atoms) and excreting (losing atoms).

cues.zh: 比起“卡蒂萨克号”——一艘殖民时期的茶叶船，被烧毁后用新部件修复。
cues.en: Compare to the "The Cutty Sark", a colonial tea ship burned down and restored with new parts.

cues.zh: 它还是原来那艘“卡蒂萨克号”吗？
cues.en: Is it still the same "Cutty Sark"?

cues.zh: 结果是一样的：全是新部件——只是花费的时间不同。
cues.en: The result is the same: all new parts - only the time it took is different.

cues.zh: 如果你乐意在生活中玩“忒修斯之船”（你其实已经在这么做了）……
cues.en: If you're happy "Ship of Theseus"-ing through life (as you already do), ...

cues.zh: ……那么被传送“卡蒂萨克号”化一下也不该有所谓。对吧……？
cues.en: ...then getting "Cutty Sark"-ed by transport shouldn't matter. Right...?

cues.zh: 然而……走进一台分解器坏掉的运作中的传送机——死亡就暴露了：
cues.en: However... step into a working transporter with a broken disassembler - and death is revealed:

cues.zh: ……传送前和传送后的你可以就“谁是你”产生分歧。
cues.en: ...pre-transport and post-transport you can disagree on who is you.

cues.zh: 而当 Scotty 对传送前的你说“抱歉，分解器坏了，给我们一分钟修一下”，你是不会干等着不动的。
cues.en: And when Scotty tells pre-transport you "Sorry, the disassembler is broken, give us a minute to fix it", you aren't going to wait around.

cues.zh: 你的一个副本抵达了目的地，这并不能带来安慰。
cues.en: That a copy of you made it to the destination is no consolation.

cues.zh: 传送器必须是个自杀箱。
cues.en: The transporter has to be a suicide box.

cues.zh: 那么，为什么要担心虚构技术的形而上学含义呢？
cues.en: OK, so why worry about the metaphysical implications of fictional technology?

cues.zh: 因为传送器把我们引向了意识的问题。
cues.en: Because the transporter points us to the problem of consciousness.

cues.zh: 我们之前很快就排除了不可测量之物的想法——因为关于复制品，我们能测量的一切都是相同的……
cues.en: We were quick to cut out the idea of the unmeasurable before -- because everything we can measure about the copy is identical...

cues.zh: ……但确实有某种无法测量的不同之处。
cues.en: ...but there is something unmeasurably different.

cues.zh: 传送器迫使我们直面一种可能性：作为有意识的生物，存在着某种无法从外部测量的东西。
cues.en: The transporter forces confrontation with the possibility that there's something about being a conscious creature that isn't measurable from the outside.

cues.zh: 如果我们自身不包含有意识的大脑，又怎能知道其他大脑是有意识的呢？
cues.en: Did we not contain conscious brains ourselves, how would we know that other brains are conscious?

cues.zh: 说实话，你真正能确定的只有*你自己*是有意识的……
cues.en: Truth be told, you can really only know that *you* are conscious...

cues.zh: ——而给他人以善意的信任，似乎是一种礼貌。
cues.en: -- and it seems polite to give other people the benefit of the doubt.

cues.zh: 但要是有一台电脑声称自己有意识，你又怎么能知道呢？
cues.en: But were a computer to claim that it was conscious, how would you know?

cues.zh: 你连绵不断的意识流，就是你的生命。
cues.en: Your continuous stream of consciousness is your life.

cues.zh: 只有你自己能体会到它，能知晓它是否“存在”，以及它是否是连续的。
cues.en: And you are the only one who can experience it, who can know if it *exists* and if it is continuous.

cues.zh: 而传送机之所以可怕，是因为它切断了这种意识。
cues.en: And transporters are scary because they cause breaks in that consciousness.

cues.zh: 它造出了一个复制品，去过你留下的人生，没人能察觉到异样。
cues.en: Making a copy that lives the life that you have left, with no one the wiser.

cues.zh: 而且根本不可能有人察觉到。
cues.en: With no one able to be wiser.

cues.zh: 虽然传送机不是真的，但意识的中断却是真实的。
cues.en: And while transporters aren't real, breaks in consciousness are.

cues.zh: 如果你去做手术，被全身麻醉后，你根本无法确定醒来的是不是原本的你。
cues.en: If you go for surgery, when they put you under, you can't be sure if it's you that woke up.

cues.zh: 照这么说，你的床可能就是一台自杀机器。
cues.en: For that matter, your bed might be a suicide machine.

cues.zh: 每晚陷入无意识的沉睡，都是死神温暖的拥抱……
cues.en: Every night's slip into unconsciousness, the warm embrace of the reaper...

cues.zh: ……而每个清晨，都是一个全新造物意识生命中，最初也是唯一的开端。
cues.en: ...and every morning the first and only day of a new creature's conscious life.

cues.zh: 这无从知晓。
cues.en: It's impossible to know.

cues.zh: 今晚好好睡吧。
cues.en: Sleep well tonight.

cues.zh: 感谢观看。如果你喜欢本集的画作，Patreon上有特别壁纸。
cues.en: Thanks for watching. If you enjoyed this episode's artwork there are special wallpapers over at Patreon.

cues.zh: 点击这里获取《星际迷航》壁纸……
cues.en: So click here to get access to the Star Trek wallpapers...

cues.zh: ……感谢你支持本频道，帮助制作这类定制画作。
cues.en: ...and thank you for supporting the channel to help get this kind of custom artwork made.

cues.zh: 还在看？
cues.en: Still here?

cues.zh: 你不可能永远保持清醒。
cues.en: You can't stay awake forever.
